label: letter i input at original positions 0-3
explanation: Token-and-position feature: fires when the input token is the letter i during the original (pre-DEL) phase at early positions t=0..3. It has perfect precision on dev, and 99.5% of activation mass. Magnitude depends on position: about 0.86 of max at t=0, 1.0 at t=1, about 0.83 at t=2, and about 0.4 at t=3. At t=4 it drops to a trace (about 0.02-0.07), and it is silent from t=5 on. It does not fire on other tokens apart from trace activations (about 0.01-0.02) on y/r/e/d right after an i, and it is silent on the delimiter. It is almost entirely silent in the copy phase, even when i is fed back as an input there (only rare traces). Repeated i at early positions still fires (e.g. a second i at t=2 is about 0.85).

issues: Small nit: the explanation says the y/r/e/d trace activations come 'right after an i', but one test miss is 'j [r:0.02]' at t=1, with no i before it. It is a trace activation (0.02) and holds no meaningful mass.

No real gap: the recall misses (9507 test steps, 0.5% of mass) are all trace activations, mostly i at t=4 at 0.02-0.07. Widening the predicate to t<=4 lowers F1 (0.920 vs 0.933, precision 0.896), so t<=3 is the better boundary.

Every claim checked out. Test precision is 1.0 with 0 false positives. There are 0 activations on the delimiter. The copy phase has 207 of 76101 dev activations. Copy-phase i inputs reach precision 0.002 and mass 0.00015, so i fed back there does not fire it. Mass by position is t0 0.28, t1 0.32, t2 0.26, t3 0.13, t4 0.004, so t=1 is the peak, as stated. Repeated i fires: an i at t=2 right after another i has precision 1.0, and non-first i at t<=3 has precision 1.0.
